name: Forty Thieves
description: Forty Thieves, also known as 'Napoleon at St. Helena' or 'Roosevelt at San Juan', is a notoriously difficult and strategic two-deck Solitaire game. Requiring 104 cards, the game challenges players to organize a vast tableau of 40 cards into eight separate foundations. Unlike many solitaires, building in the tableau must be done strictly by suit and in descending order. Because the stock can only be cycled through once, and only a single card is drawn at a time, players must exercise extreme caution to avoid blocking their own win path.

content.text: Forty Thieves, also known as 'Napoleon at St. Helena' or 'Roosevelt at San Juan', is a notoriously difficult and strategic two-deck Solitaire game. Requiring 104 cards, the game challenges players to organize a vast tableau of 40 cards into eight separate foundations. Unlike many solitaires, building in the tableau must be done strictly by suit and in descending order. Because the stock can only be cycled through once, and only a single card is drawn at a time, players must exercise extreme caution to avoid blocking their own win path.

The game gained legendary status as the favorite pastime of Napoleon Bonaparte during his exile on the island of Saint Helena. Its name refers to the 40 cards dealt into the initial tableau, resembling a gathered band of thieves guarding their treasure.

One player only. Forty Thieves is a patience (solitaire) game; the single player plays against the layout, moving cards from the tableau and stock to the eight foundations. There are no opponents or partnerships.
Two standard decks shuffled together (104 cards).
